stories.title: Tomorrow: TechCrunch Founder Summit takes over Boston and when pass rates increase
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is selling passes to a business conference in Boston. Prices are going up tomorrow morning.
stories.why_it_matters: This only matters if you want to attend a tech industry conference. There's nothing you need to do otherwise.

stories.title: Artificial Intelligence Resurrections Are Becoming Big Business, But Who Really Benefits From Bringing Back The Dead?
stories.simple_summary: Companies are now offering services that use AI to create digital versions of people who have died. The headline asks who actually benefits from this.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a new technology that exists, but it's not something most people will encounter in their daily life.

stories.title: Apple Watch’s AI features for rewinding and recapping conversations begin beta testing
stories.simple_summary: Apple watches will soon have AI features that listen to conversations and remind you what was said. Apple is testing this now before releasing it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own an Apple Watch, you may get a tool to help you remember important details from conversations without taking notes yourself.

stories.title: ‘A serious failure’: CPS prosecutor cites imaginary case to high court after AI search
stories.simple_summary: A lawyer in Chicago used an AI search tool to find a court case but the AI made up a case that doesn't exist. The lawyer presented this fake case to a court.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI tools can seem confident while giving you completely false information, so you cannot trust them to do legal research or important work without checking their answers.

stories.title: America’s AI Ambitions Depend on Taiwan
stories.simple_summary: The United States needs Taiwan to make advanced computer chips, which are essential for building powerful AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and government leaders. It doesn't directly affect your daily life right now.

stories.title: Anthropic Claims to Be Near Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, a company that makes AI, says it is getting close to creating AI that can improve itself without human help.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to AI researchers and investors tracking the industry. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses
stories.simple_summary: Google has a tool called Dreambeans that uses AI to create personal stories. Google just added the ability to use it in 13 Indian languages.
stories.why_it_matters: If you speak an Indian language and want to create personalized AI-written stories, this tool is now available to you.

stories.title: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps
stories.simple_summary: Apple is looking for ways to make money by working with other companies' AI apps. The company hasn't announced specifics yet.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching Apple's business strategy. It doesn't affect you unless you're an app developer.

stories.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens
stories.simple_summary: A powerful person at a startup company uses AI tools so much that he pays $200,000 per year to use them. He says he loves AI so much he barely sleeps.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about one person's expensive hobby with AI tools. Most small business owners don't spend anywhere near this amount.

stories.title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
stories.simple_summary: A new company called Trajectory raised $45 million from investors. The company makes AI training easier for people without technical skills.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people developing AI. There's nothing you need to do unless you're involved in AI development.

stories.title: Law firm's AI use doesn't warrant cutting legal fees, US appeals court rules
stories.simple_summary: A court ruled that when a law firm uses AI to help with its work, the firm cannot charge lower fees to clients just because AI made the work cheaper.
stories.why_it_matters: If you hire a lawyer, this means the law firm's use of AI tools probably won't lower your bill. The savings stay with the firm.

stories.title: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, an AI company, is warning that AI is getting so advanced that it may soon be able to improve itself automatically and grow extremely powerful very quickly.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an important concern for AI researchers and policy makers. Most ordinary people won't notice changes in their day-to-day life yet.
